hypotheses.paper: a conic structure at p (the commented-out draft's ray condition)

findings: DESIGN NOTE (draft, not a paper claim; source: draft material commented out in these.tex (l.3560–3677), not part of the thesis): the draft's proposition (these.tex:3645), read literally with the draft's ray-only conic structure (these.tex:3569), fails; counterexample motivating the radius hypothesis of GX.ConicStructure: GX.celestial_counterexample gives X = susp(Bool) (homeomorphic to R), G = Perm Bool acting radially (analytic, G = G_p, checked in GX.celestial_counterexample_hypotheses), the full chart phi(b,r) = (b, rho'(b) r) with rho'(true)=1, rho'(false)=1/2 (ray-compatible, inducing the natural action on the link Bool), and Sigma = a point: the two cone charts reach radii 1 and 2 at the same point while G preserves radii, so the cone preatlas is not a (G,X)-atlas. The draft's step these.tex:3667 '(phi_p g phi_p^-1)(phi_i(x), r) = (g phi_i(x), r)' is exactly the radial hypothesis. Proved for the corrected notion: for a conic structure conjugating each h to susp(h|L) (GX.ConicStructure) and full, the cone preatlas is an a.e. (G,X)-atlas whose chart changes lie in H.

DESIGN NOTE: radius preservation is SUFFICIENT, NOT NECESSARY. Example (auditor's, BBS-Celestial AUDIT-1): X = R, G = Aff(R) (analytic), p = 0, H = G_p (all x -> a x), phi = the inverse sphere map with V = R (S(R) = {+1, -1}), Sigma = a point with its two charts to +1 and -1 (a (G_p, X_p)-atlas, a < 0 swapping +-1). The two cone charts are r -> r and r -> -r, their chart change -id lies in G, so the cone preatlas IS a (G,X)-atlas; but no radius-preserving conic structure exists for H = G_p, which contains x -> x/2 (GX.isEmpty_conicStructure_affine_stabilizer, BBS-Affine; the atlas half is not formalized). The draft's argument at these.tex:3667 needs only a RADIAL LIFT: for each h in H some g_h in G with phi(g_h x) = susp(h.)(phi x); radius preservation is the case g_h = h, and the two coincide when G is contained in Isom (Euclidean or Poincare). This is a candidate minimal hypothesis for the author; this round keeps radius preservation in GX.ConicStructure and does not attempt the generalisation.

The draft's argument computes on all of (U_i cap U_j) x R+*, i.e. uses that phi_p g phi_p^-1 = susp(g) on the WHOLE cone; with phi only equivariant on U cap g^-1 U this needs an argument: GX.ConicStructure.map_smul_of_isFull (a full conic structure is H-invariant on U, by real induction along rays).

labels.label: rem:regular_rays (RamcovGX.tex:740, 'the image of regular (G,X)-manifolds are regular except possibly at O and are regular at O iff Sigma is homeomorphic to a sphere')

hypotheses.note: the 'if' half at O proved for Sigma = the model link L itself (with its tautological (H,L)-structure); the 'only if' half not stated

CompactSpace L, ADDED for mem_reg_of_mk_mem_reg / mk_mem_sing / mk_mem_reg_iff only: phi^-1(L x [t/2, 2t]) is then compact, hence closed in the T2 space X, so g^-1 psi (a limit of points of it) lands in U. Every intended link is compact (S^n, HS^2 = S^2); the non-compact statement is open (possibly false).

findings: (a) the ray over a regular point of Sigma is regular: proved (mk_mem_reg). (b) the ray over a singular point is singular: proved for a compact link (mem_reg_of_mk_mem_reg, mk_mem_sing, together mk_mem_reg_iff), WITHOUT invariance of domain, on the auditor's route: a chart psi of the maximal atlas at (x,t) is, on the regular part of a box B x ]l,u[ (preconnected because Reg Sigma is portly), g0 h . phi^-1 o susp*(e) for ONE g0 in G (a connectedness argument, IsPreconnected.induction2', with G's rigidity); so F = phi o g0^-1 o psi preserves the radius there and, by density and continuity, on the whole box; compactness puts g0^-1 psi inside U; then z -> pi F(z,t) is an open partial homeomorphism of Sigma at x (F is a homeomorphism of the box onto an open set and preserves r), compatible with Sigma's maximal atlas (IsMaximalAEAtlas.mem_of_compatible). (c) the apex is regular when Sigma is the model link L: proved (apex_mem_reg_model). The converse at O ('regular at O only if Sigma is the model / a sphere') is NOT stated: in this generality (arbitrary (G,X), arbitrary H <= G_p) it is unclear it holds; BBS's form is BBS-Q4.
questions: Is the non-compact case of 'the ray over a singular point is singular' wanted? The proof here uses CompactSpace L only to keep g^-1 psi inside U; without it the statement as written is unproved and possibly false.

kb_proposals: To put a point into a maximal a.e. atlas, insert the chart into an a.e. atlas A, prove the insert is IsGXAtlas via isGXAtlas_of_eventually (four cases with rcases on insert), then subset_maximalAEAtlas hA' (hGX.isThinner_completion_of_subset (subset_insert _ _)) - no need for IsMaximalAEAtlas.mem_of_compatible (which requires compatibility with ALL charts of the maximal atlas).

A singular (H,L)-structure on a point or on the model space is cheapest through SingularGXStructure.ofHasGroupoid with a one-chart ChartedSpace; membership of further charts then follows from mem_maximalAtlas_iff_eventually.

To show a ray (x,t) regular in a suspension forces x regular, do not reach for invariance of domain: pin ONE g0 on the regular part of a box by IsPreconnected.induction2' (the set of g with psi = g h . coneChart e near a point is locally constant), get radius preservation of phi o g0^-1 o psi by density (mem_closure_image into a closed diagonal), and read the chart on the slice r = t (GX.ConicStructure.mem_reg_of_mk_mem_reg).
